subjects.displayTitle: Reading the sacred writings: words that become a life
subjects.introduction: Recite the verses of God morning and evening, Bahá’u’lláh commands, and then qualifies the command in a way that overturns every quantitative habit: what counts is the love and inclination of the soul, so that a single verse read with spirit and joy outweighs many books read without them. The Tablets are to be read with a melodious voice and the tone of the heart, pondered until their hidden pearls come up from the depths, and above all practised, since to hold the Book and not act on it is to miss its purpose. There is a warning too: people who recited scripture day and night were veiled, when its Revealer appeared, by their attachment to the words themselves. The Psalmist’s tree planted by water, bearing fruit in season because its roots drink from meditation on the law day and night, pictures the same slow nourishment [1]. The journey continues into contemplation and meditation, into disciplined study and deepening, and into the Word of God itself.
subjects.arc: Begin with joyful attention, join understanding to practice, and explore the shared disciplines that keep reading alive.

order.why: Enjoins regular recitation while preferring a single verse read with joy to mechanical quantity.
Open with quality of attention rather than quantity.
Introduce reflection as drawing out hidden pearls.
Bring the words into practice at once.
Challenge familiarity that conceals the Revealer.
State the purpose of understanding inner significance.
Read study through the image of polishing diamonds.
Make room for illumination and tranquility.
shortened: Read ye the Tablets, that breasts may be illumined thereby and hearts may find tranquility.

order.why: Hear the part played by melody and the heart.
shortened: Read the Tablets of His Holiness Baha'u'llah with a good melody, peruse them with the tone of the heart and of the spirit. It will confer life, it will quicken the dead and it will grant the power of light to every broken-winged bird and cause it to sing and chant.

order.why: Join recitation with joy.
shortened: Read ye the verses of God with joy and fragrance - they draw you to the Most Exalted Horizon and bring you near to the sublime station.

order.why: Read the invitation to a melodious voice.
shortened: When thou attainest unto a Tablet of thy Lord, read what is therein with the most melodious voice. It will attract thee to an exalted station.

order.why: Consider listening as a human capacity.
shortened: In truth, in the first station and primary rank, the faculty of hearing was created solely for hearkening unto the blessed Word.

order.why: Connect reflection with awakening and assurance.
Join pondering with a daily rhythm.
Retain the source’s daily invitation to reflect.
Read diligence in pondering alongside recitation.
shortened: At all times occupy thyself with the recitation of the verses of God and be diligent in pondering His firm utterances.

order.why: Consider discovery of the intended meaning.
Join reflection with fairness of judgment.
shortened: Say: Ponder, O people, on the Revelation of God and His sovereignty and His greatness and His power. Then judge with fairness and be not of those who have disbelieved in God, the Mighty, the Beloved. Rejoice in what hath been sent down unto thee in this Tablet, then recite it at all times. By My life, through it thou shalt find the fragrance of the Garment wafting from this exalted Station.

order.why: Read discernment between revelation and heedless speech.
shortened: Read thou My verses and ponder that which hath been sent down from the heaven of My Will and that which every heedless and veiled one uttereth.

order.why: Consider the transforming possibility of one fair reading.
shortened: By God's life! Were the people of the earth to peruse but a single Tablet from among the divine Tablets with justice and fairness, they would all turn toward the Most Exalted Horizon and return from that which they possess unto that which is God's.

order.why: Widen study to the Qur’an and Gospel.
Hear the reported encouragement to comprehend both Testaments.
Include children in a broad scriptural education.
shortened: Encourage other children also to drink from this Salsabil spring and partake of this pure water.
O Lord! Assist his peers and equals to learn knowledge and wisdom and to study the Torah and Gospel and Qur'an and examine the Bayan and manifest wisdom and understanding.

order.why: Connect study of religions with considerate publication.
shortened: The Bible and Holy Books of other religions must always be studied and to be read in the Baha'i meetings. Their study will widen the circle of one's information and acquaint him with the wonderful prophecies fulfilled today. A Baha'i publication must never publish anything which may cause provocations or injure the feelings of any one or displease any soul. It must publish such matters that would be conducive to the happiness, hopefulness, advancement, guidance and illumination of the readers.

order.why: Keep the reported question to a Christian reader in context.
Read the example of careful Qur’anic recitation and inquiry.
shortened: He would recite the Qur'an with careful pronunciation and would delve deep into the meanings of this Noble Book morning and night, finding in its verses the fountain of living waters and guidance to the path of salvation.

order.why: Hear the reported consolation found in prophetic lives.
Consider language learning and translation.
Join language proficiency with understanding.
shortened: Strive to properly learn the Persian language so that you may recite the Tablets of Baha'u'llah and understand their meanings.

order.why: Read the wish for direct access to the writings.
shortened: I ask God to make you proficient and learned in the language of the people of the East so that you may read by yourself from the writings of your Lord, the Merciful, the Compassionate.

order.why: Keep the counsel concerning Persian and Arabic.
shortened: Move among the handmaidens with perfect dignity and composure, and persist in reading the verses of God in Persian and Arabic, for this shall be the cause of eternal life.

order.why: Introduce memorization as a valued practice.
Join shared reading with remembering vital points.
Read gatherings as a place where love is kindled.
shortened: The friends in every land should gather together with wisdom and utterance in meetings and assemblies to read the verses of God, for the verses kindle the fire of love and ignite its flame.

order.why: Consider the instruction to read and meditate together or alone.
Read the encouragement to continue a shared study.
Connect learning proofs with the capacity to guide.
shortened: I hope that night and day you will strive with heart and soul, closing your eyes to all else, so that with a free heart and gladdened spirit you may pursue divine knowledge and heavenly mysteries, may become informed of divine proofs and aware of clear evidences, may open your tongue to guide souls, may lead multitudes to the shore of the sea of grace, and may illumine eyes with the light of guidance.

order.why: Consider the particular instruction to study letters to rulers.
shortened: It behooveth thee to read the blessed Surih of Ra'is, as well as the Tablets to the Kings, and what befell the Chief of Paris.

It is most strange that your honor hath not seen the divine Tablets, for had you observed them, you would have become aware of the power and might of God and would have spoken words that would convince that person and his like.

order.why: Turn a specific question toward the Book of Certitude.
shortened: Beware lest the affairs of the world grieve thee or prevent thee from Him Who is the Creator of heaven. Abandon every matter and hold fast unto the Cause of God, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy. And concerning what thou didst ask about the return- read thou the Kitab-i-Iqan which the All-Merciful revealed when the Light was shining from the horizon of Iraq. Thus doth the Lord of all horizons command thee from His exalted station.

order.why: Keep the related reading of community news distinct from scripture.
Return to knowing what has been revealed.
shortened: Read thou the Book of God that thou mayest know what hath been sent down from His wondrous Kingdom.

order.why: Consider revealed utterance as a guide and teacher.
shortened: Whatsoever hath been revealed from the Supreme Pen is a lamp for the guidance of the servants and a guide and teacher for those in all lands. The recitation of any of these will be beloved and will become the cause and means of the outpourings of the Lord of all being.

order.why: Hear the Bab’s extended account of the gifts of the Bayan.
Read the value attributed to each word and letter.
shortened: By the life of God! Every word thereof is the quickener of the dead and the manifestation of signs, and every letter thereof is, in the sight of God, more precious than all things.

order.why: Consider the invitation to discover what was hidden.
Read in a condition of detachment.
Hear the call to draw near through reading.
Read the counsel given upon receiving a Tablet.
shortened: When thou art honored with God's Tablet, recite it by night and by day. Verily it will draw thee nigh unto the most exalted station.

order.why: Join daily recitation with steadfast direction.
Consider the Book as protection and nearness.
shortened: Hold fast unto the Book of thy Lord, then recite it by night and by day. It shall verily protect thee and draw thee nigh unto the Most Sublime Vision.

order.why: Read preservation and repetition as safeguards against heedlessness.
shortened: Preserve thou this Tablet and recite it most days lest thou become heedless of what God hath willed for thee therein and be of them that are detached.

order.why: Hear gratitude expressed in repeated reading.
shortened: Know thou the worth of what hath been sent down and dispatched to thee, then recite it morning and evening, nay rather at all times.

order.why: Join care for a Tablet with sharing its fragrance.
Read steadfastness, detachment, and recurring encounter together.
Consider what reading creates within the heart.
shortened: Preserve the Tablet of God, then read what hath been revealed therein by night and by day, that it may create within thy heart that which will draw thee nigh unto a mighty and exalted station.

order.why: Keep preservation joined with joy.
Read the warning against neglect.
shortened: Preserve what hath been sent down to thee from the heaven of grace, then recite it throughout the days and be not of the heedless ones.

order.why: Consider the effect of recitation upon one’s life among others.
shortened: Preserve thou God's Tablet and recite what hath been revealed therein that thy face may be illumined thereby amongst all peoples.

order.why: Hear the daily rhythm of reading and praise.
shortened: We have indeed inhaled the fragrance of thy turning unto Us, and have revealed for thee this mighty Book. Read it by night and by day, then glorify thy Lord with praise at morn and at eventide.

order.why: Read remembrance at evening and dawn.
shortened: Take hold of the Book of God with the power that proceedeth from Him, then make mention of Him at eventide and at dawn.

order.why: Consider reliance upon divine power in holding the Book.
Return to recitation and praise morning and evening.
shortened: Thus have We sent down the verses unto you and dispatched them to you, that you may be of the thankful. Recite them morning and evening, and glorify your Lord with praise at daybreak and eventide.

order.why: Hear another invitation to sustained gratitude.
Join glad tidings with the abundance of verses.
shortened: Rejoice in the glad-tidings of thy Lord, then recite what hath been sent down unto thee of the verses which the peoples of the world are powerless to enumerate.

order.why: Consider the attraction of hearts through reading.
Read the Book as guidance toward a higher station.
Let repeated reading deepen recognition.
shortened: O Nasru'llah! When thou hast attained unto the Tablet of thy Lord, read it again and again, that thou mayest inhale the fragrance of the verses of thy Lord and be of them who have detached themselves in His love from all directions.

order.why: Hear the collective invitation to hold the Tablet.
shortened: Take hold, O My loved ones, of the Tablet of God with a power from Him, then recite it by night and by day.

order.why: Consider continuity in the practice of reading.
shortened: Take hold of the Book of God with the power that comes from Him, then recite it at all times.

order.why: Read preservation and recitation toward transformed perception.
Join study explicitly with living the teachings.
shortened: I wish you to study the works of the Blessed Beauty and to live according to His teaching.

order.why: Read holding the Book together with acting upon it.
shortened: Hold fast unto the Book of God, then act according to what is therein, and take hold of the hem of His Name, the All-Forgiving.

order.why: Move from what has been read to what is done.
Join remembrance and following the guidance.
shortened: Remember Him by night and by day, then follow what He has revealed in the scriptures and tablets.

order.why: End with deeds and character as the means of reaching hearts.
shortened: The honored Siyyid Taqi, glory be upon him, appeared before the Wronged One with thy letter. We heard thy call and made mention of thee with a mention whose fragrance shall endure as long as the divine Kingdom endures. In all conditions We have counseled the servants to trustworthiness and religious devotion. In truth, the hosts that assist this Most Great Cause have been and are goodly deeds and praiseworthy character. Blessed are they who, through these hosts, open the cities of hearts in the name of the True One, exalted be His glory.

questions: What changes when the value of reading is measured by spirit, joy, and understanding rather than by volume?
How might recitation, reflection, memorization, and practice support one another without becoming mechanical?
What could make familiarity with a scripture a veil, and how might a reader remain open to fresh recognition?
What does studying the scriptures of several religions ask of a reader’s attention and humility?
How does Psalm 1’s image of a nourished tree illuminate the fruits of sustained reading?
What signs in conduct, conversation, or service might show that a passage has begun to shape a life?

references.label: 1 · Psalm 1:1–3 · Meditation and the fruit-bearing tree
references.note: The King James Version links delight in divine law and meditation day and night with a tree planted beside water that bears fruit in season. Read this image beside the compilation’s emphasis on joyful recitation, patient reflection, and action. What kinds of nourishment and fruit are being imagined, and how might the image resist a purely quantitative approach to study?

subjects.displayTitle: Apocalyptic imagery: upheaval, unveiling, and renewal
subjects.introduction: The sun darkens, the moon is cleft, the stars fall and the mountains walk, and Bahá’u’lláh asks the one who hesitates whether the signs have not already been sent down. His claim is startling in its plainness: the Hour has struck, the Resurrection has come to pass, and the heaven that was torn open was the heaven of idle fancies in the minds of men. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá hears in the second blast of the trumpet the stirring of spiritual life, and the Báb describes a Day that comes suddenly, when the earth casts forth its burdens and each soul sees what it has laid up. Beside the quaking earth stand gardens, flowing springs and the righteous singing, for judgment and renewal arrive together. The Qur’án’s own sequence, in which cosmic disturbance ends with every soul knowing what it has brought, keeps moral accountability in view [1]. Why so vast an event could pass unnoticed by those it addresses remains the haunting question. From here the road leads into the imagery of the Qur’án and the reading of symbols, and on to the forces of integration and disintegration at work in a world convulsed.
subjects.arc: Begin with unveiling and renewed life, listen to the full force of the images, and return to recognition, judgment, and steadfast hope.

order.why: Read the passage’s own description of emblems.
shortened: The path hath become smooth, the way straightened, the carpet of the Kingdom is spread, the Tabernacle hath been elevated upon the Hill of Might, the powers of heaven have been shaken, the corners of the earth have quaked, the sun has been darkened, the moon ceased to give light, the stars have fallen, the nations of the earth have lamented, and the Son of Man hath come upon the clouds of heaven with power and great glory, and He hath sent His angels with the sound of the great trumpet, and no one knows the meaning of these emblems save the wise and informed.

order.why: Open with resurrection as continuing regeneration.
shortened: Nevertheless, O Questioner! Hearken unto My voice which sayeth: "Open thine eyes that thou mayest behold the Most Great Beauty, through Whom speaketh the Lord of divine decree. By God! Through Him the 'Hour' hath appeared, and the 'Resurrection' hath come to pass, and the 'Moon' hath been cleft asunder and thou wouldst behold all in a 'continuing Regeneration' if thou be of them that possess insight.

order.why: Make the heaven of idle fancies explicit.
shortened: Say: O people! Do ye hesitate concerning Him by Whom the heaven was cleft asunder, the moon was split, and the Caller called out from the direction of a mighty throne? Have not the signs been sent down? Have not the tokens appeared? By God! The heaven of idle fancies hath been split and the All-Merciful hath come, surrounded by hosts of revelation and inspiration.

order.why: Consider the second blast as spiritual life.
shortened: This is why He says: "Then there shall be another blast, and lo! they shall rise and gaze around them: And the earth shall shine with the light of her Lord." And from the second blast, spiritual realities and celestial essences shall find life and shall be set in motion by the dawning of the Sun of Truth. This second blast is the appearance of the Ancient Beauty, "Him Whom God shall make manifest."

order.why: Explore the two blasts through negation and affirmation.
Read the interpretation of the two witnesses.
Consider the woman in Revelation through an attributed interpretation.
Allow an explicitly deferred explanation to remain open.
Preserve the different claim and setting of the Bab’s letter.
Hear the Bab’s full sequence of judgment images.
shortened: When Our Cause cometh, it shall come upon you suddenly, with mighty truth. Verily this Day is the truth from your Lord.

On that Day ye shall not possess even a particle of knowledge from the Book, cut off in truth by the truth. The Kingdom on that Day shall belong in truth to the All-Merciful, and ye shall not be able to utter a word, nay not even a whisper.

Verily We have ordained upon the earth its quaking, and none can turn back God's true command save that the earth cast forth its burdens. On that Day shall man witness what hath been on earth of its possessions.

order.why: Read the overwhelming cascade as a question.
Follow the extended proclamation of fulfilled signs.
Hold the scenes of upheaval and adorned gardens together.
shortened: The Hour hath come to pass, the Resurrection, the gathering and raising of the dead have appeared, the earth hath quaked, the seas have boiled, the heaven hath been cleft asunder, the sun hath been folded up, the stars have been scattered, the Balance hath been set up, the Bridge hath been extended, the fires have been kindled, Paradise hath been brought nigh, the palaces have been adorned, the gardens have been embellished, and the fountains have gushed forth, the trees have been beautified in this witnessed Day.

order.why: Hear the rapid alternation of life and disturbance.
shortened: Lo! The gardens have been adorned! The Kawthar and Salsabil have gushed forth! The dove hath warbled! The birds have sung! The lions have roared! The fish have swum! The earth hath quaked! The mountains have moved! The seas have boiled! The heaven hath been cleft! The sun hath been folded up! The stars have been scattered! The Hour hath arrived! The great catastrophe hath appeared! Paradise hath been brought near! The Fire hath been kindled!

order.why: Read the juxtaposition of joy and loss.
Notice illumination emerging amid shattered structures.
Connect resurrection with protection, balance, and guidance.
Hear the invitation to drink and receive fragrance.
Turn cosmic trembling into a prayer for gladness.
shortened: I entreat Thee by Thy Name through which the Hour hath struck, and the Resurrection came to pass, and fear and trembling seized all that are in heaven and all that are on earth, to rain down, out of the heaven of Thy mercy and the clouds of Thy tender compassion, what will gladden the hearts of Thy servants, who have turned towards Thee and helped Thy Cause.

order.why: Ask for steadfastness within the proclamation.
shortened: I beseech Thee by the Name through which the trumpet was sounded and the dwellers of the graves arose, and through which Beauty was made manifest and the mountains were set in motion, to grant me the Kawthar of bounty from the hands of Thy favors and the choice wine of steadfastness through Thy grace and sovereignty.

order.why: Read gratitude for firmness amid disruption.
shortened: And say: Praise be unto Thee for having bestowed Thy favor upon this servant of Thine and guided him to the straight path, and made firm the foundation, and granted success in remaining steadfast on a Day when the pillars of all created things were shaken, and the hearts of all beings were set ablaze, and every pregnant one cast forth her burden, and every nursing mother became heedless of the child she was nursing.

order.why: Keep the passage’s terror and human vulnerability audible.
shortened: This is the terror of resurrection and the horror of loss in this world and the next! This is the fear when every pregnant woman shall lay down her burden, the dread when every nursing mother shall forget her nursling, and the terror when thou shalt see mankind as in a drunken state, yet they are not drunk: but severe is the chastisement of God!

order.why: Hear the trumpet and the trembling of hearts.
shortened: Say: By God! The blast hath been blown on the trumpet, and lo, mankind hath swooned away before us! The Herald hath cried out, and the Summoner raised His voice saying: "The Kingdom is God's, the Most Powerful, the Help in Peril, the Self-Subsisting."

This is the Day on which all eyes shall stare up with terror, the Day in which the hearts of them that dwell on earth shall tremble, save them whom thy Lord, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise, pleaseth to deliver.

order.why: Notice the emphatic shift from asking to proclaiming.
shortened: O Most Generous, Most Glorious One! Have the verses been sent down? Say: Yea, by the Lord of the heavens! Has the Hour come? Nay, it has passed, and the Manifestor of clear proofs has come. The Inevitable has come to pass and the Truth has come with proof and evidence. The Wakeful One has appeared and creation is in turmoil and agitation. The earthquakes have come and the tribes have wailed out of fear of God, the Mighty, the Compelling. Say: The Deafening Blast has cried out and this Day belongs to God, the One, the Chosen.

order.why: Connect the great event with the establishment of the Cause.
shortened: He hath arisen to establish His Cause with a power whereby the Resurrection hath come to pass, the Hour hath struck, the Reality hath appeared and the Great Calamity hath occurred.

order.why: Read the sounding of the trumpet and its exception.
shortened: By the life of God! The Hour hath come, and the Sure Truth hath appeared, and the Trump hath sounded, and the Trumpet hath been blown, and all who are in the heavens and on earth have swooned away, save those whom thy Lord, the Almighty, the All-Powerful, hath willed.

order.why: Hear the related sequence of cry, balance, and blast.
shortened: By God! The Cry hath been raised, the mountains have passed away, the Balance hath been set up, the Trumpet hath been blown, and all who are in earth and heaven have swooned away, save whom God, the Almighty, the All-Powerful, hath willed.

order.why: Read the address to Israfil and the speaking of atoms.
shortened: O Israfil! By the life of God, the Trumpet hath been sounded, and all who are in the heavens and on the earth have swooned away, save only certain letters of the face of thy Lord, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.
The Balance hath been set up and the Path laid down, and the Cry hath been raised in truth, and every atom hath spoken forth.

order.why: Consider trumpet, bell, and bugle as proclamation.
Hear their shared announcement of sovereignty.
Read the ocean and atoms as witnesses.
shortened: This is a Day wherein the Most Great Ocean hath surged, and the atoms have cried out: The Kingdom is God's, the Almighty, the All-Bountiful!

order.why: Let light, trumpet, and moving mountains form a concise sequence.
shortened: Say: O people! The light hath shone forth and the trumpet hath been blown and the mountains have been moved.

order.why: Read the summons within the eclipsed lights.
Hear the appeal to perceive what is proclaimed.
shortened: The sun hath risen, the moon hath been cleft, and the stars have fallen, would that ye perceived.

order.why: Consider the disturbance at the moment of appearance.
Read desolation in the image of abandoned houses.
Hear the earthquake as a test of nearness.
Read the balance established amid shaking earth.
Consider the response that distinguishes the addressee.
shortened: Say: O people! This is the Day wherein the heaven hath been cleft asunder, and the earth hath been rent, and the skin hath crept with fear, save of him who hath answered his Lord and turned toward this outstretched Shadow.

order.why: Hear the Lord’s coming amid the signs.
Explains how literal expectations of apocalyptic signs can obstruct recognition.
Retain the language of chastisement in its own setting.
shortened: O thou who art attracted by the fragrances of God! The trumpet hath been blown, and the bugle hath sounded, and the earth hath quaked, and the sun hath been folded up, and the stars have been darkened, and the seas have boiled over, and the mountains have been scattered, and the heaven hath been cleft asunder, and brought forth manifest smoke, and the people have been overwhelmed - this is a grievous chastisement.

order.why: Notice the unseen hosts within the proclamation.
Hear the reported repeated emphasis on today.
shortened: Today is the day when the heaven was rolled up. Today is the day when the sun was folded up. Today is the day when the moon was cleft asunder. Today is the day when the stars were scattered. Today is the day when the mountains moved. Today is the day when the dead came forth from their graves.

order.why: Read the compressed declaration of upheaval.
Consider creation shaken by a cry.
Read the transformation of doubters’ faces.
shortened: That which caused the kingdoms of earth and heaven to tremble hath appeared, all things were shaken, the dwellers of earth and heaven lamented, and the faces of the doubters were transformed.

order.why: Preserve the decree’s overwhelming scale.
shortened: How, then, shall I make mention of you, when the decree hath been decreed and the command established? This is a thing before which the heavens well-nigh burst, the earth is rent, and the mountains crumble to dust.

order.why: Connect eclipsed names with the will of the Revealer.
Read the promised appearance and the smiling of faith.
shortened: Say: O peoples of the earth! The All-Bountiful hath come, riding upon the clouds, while from His right the Herald of Glory proclaimeth: "O people! This is He Who was promised to you in the Books of old, and this is He at Whose appearance the Books of the peoples bowed down in submission."

The Glory shining from the horizon of My utterance be upon thee and upon those who witnessed and declared: "This is He through Whom the countenance of Faith smiled in all creation, and the Hour appeared with its signs, and the Resurrection with its mysteries."

order.why: Consider testimony to the dawning place of signs.
shortened: God testifies that there is no God but Him, and that He Who speaks is indeed the Dawning-Place of His signs and the Dayspring of His clear tokens - He at Whose appearance the heaven was cleft asunder, the earth was rent, and its peoples lamented, save whom God willed, the Lord of all worlds.

order.why: Follow the movement from promise to witnessed fulfillment.
shortened: I testify before Thee that what Thou didst promise hath appeared, what Thou didst indicate hath come to pass, and the Day which Thou didst name as the Day of God hath arrived - wherein the Trump was sounded and all who are in Thy heaven and earth were thunderstruck, save those whom the hand of Thy power did rescue. And I testify that the Bridge hath been set up and the Balance hath been established and Thy call hath been raised from the precincts of Thy prison.

order.why: Read the declaration concerning the completion of proof.
Connect response with the imagery of reckoning.
Read gathering and judgment within the community of the Bayan.
shortened: Thereupon the heavens were cleft asunder, and the earth was rent, and the mountains crumbled, and the Balance was set up, and all who were in the Bayan were gathered together. Then were the people of Paradise admitted therein, and the denizens of the Fire consigned to their abode.

order.why: Consider the image of the Crimson Ark.
Hear joy and lament as differing responses.
Ask how a proclaimed event remains unnoticed.
shortened: The mountains have passed away and the Cry hath been raised, the Trumpet hath been sounded and the Herald hath called out, yet the people are in strange stupor.

order.why: Read heedlessness beside the turning of all things toward the Prison.
shortened: The heavens have been cleft asunder, the earth hath been rent, and the mountains have crumbled, yet the people remain in heedlessness and schism. All things circle round the Prison, while the Concourse on High circle round the Throne at eventide and at dawn.

order.why: Hear the appeal to recognize the coming upon clouds.
Consider the persistence of doubt amid proclamation.
Read the opened gate and the sun beyond clouds.
shortened: The Gate hath been opened, the Doorkeeper expelled, the veils burned away, and the Sun hath shone forth from behind the clouds.

order.why: Explore one Hour presented as proof of another.
Notice the qualifying phrase in the account of resurrection.
shortened: All affairs proceed contrary to outward appearance - the mountain walketh upon the path, and from barren soil spring forth new and varied flowers. It is as though the Resurrection hath come to pass and the mysteries of the Hour been revealed.

order.why: Let the personified Hour itself become bewildered.
Retain the source’s expansive testimony and visible omission.
Keep the future tense of this proclamation.
Read the Day announced through glad tidings and weighing.
Distinguish future passing away from enduring sovereignty.
shortened: Soon shall all that is on earth perish, and sovereignty and might shall endure unto God and His chosen ones who have believed in God in this Revelation whereby the Trumpet hath been sounded and the mountains have passed away, and trembling hath seized all who are in the heavens and on earth, save those whom thy Lord, the Almighty, the All-Powerful, hath willed.

order.why: Hear the warning of a further convulsion.
shortened: Hast thou heard the Call? The foundations of the Concourse on high were shaken when the Call was raised from the Supreme Horizon, and thou seest the people reeling from the great quaking that hath caused all the powers of the earth to tremble, and which shall be followed by a mightier convulsion, more bitter and terrible.

order.why: Consider the reported expectation of justice after carnage.
shortened: As to the fifth verse: When all these brutalities are committed, when governments and nations have had enough carnage, bloodshed, destruction, then the Balances of Divine Justice will be set up.

order.why: End with counsel toward steadfastness, unity, and discernment.

questions: What becomes possible when cosmic images are read as descriptions of revelation and recognition?
How do the passages join scenes of destruction with gardens, renewed life, and glad tidings?
What differences emerge when you attend to statements of fulfillment, future expectation, and deferred explanation?
How does Qur’an 81:1–14 connect cosmic upheaval with moral accountability, and how is that connection developed here?
Why might a transformation described as universal remain unrecognized by some of those living through it?
How could these images prompt steadiness, humility, or responsible action while leaving room for what a reader does not yet understand?

references.label: 1 · Qur’an 81:1–14 · Cosmic signs and the disclosure of deeds
references.note: In the English translation displayed by Quran.com, the darkening sun, falling stars, moving mountains, and opened records lead to each soul knowing what it has brought. The passage also places the killing of infant girls under judgment. Compare its sequence with the compilation’s recurring images, attending both to moral accountability and to the distinct Babi and Baha’i interpretations of revelation and fulfillment.

subjects.displayTitle: Composition and decomposition: the changing forms of life
subjects.introduction: Nothing is ever simply destroyed. When a body is lost, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá teaches, its elements are not annihilated but released, and only because they are released can they enter new compositions: the dust of one form becomes the leaf, the animal, the human frame of another. Life, in this account, is composition and death is decomposition, and the pain of dying is the pain of leaving a form to which one had grown accustomed. Yet the elements that scatter are not the person. Against the composite and perishable body stands a spirit that is single and indivisible, and the very fact that every composition eventually dissolves becomes an argument: a joining that was neither accidental nor compelled by the elements themselves must have been willed. Socrates, in the Phaedo, asks much the same question about what is liable to dissolution and what is not [1]. The theme reaches beyond physics. Attraction and cohesion are what give a flower or a stone its existence, and discord is what ends it, so the same law is read into human fellowship, where separation is a kind of death. From here the inquiry opens into life and death, the law of transformation and change, corruption and renewal, and the old insight that things are known by their opposites.
subjects.arc: Begin with endings that enable renewal, explore the arguments about matter and spirit, and consider the possibilities and limits of the social analogy.

order.why: Follow the passage into the formation of other organisms.
Open with dissolution as a condition of new composition.
Acknowledge the pain attached to losing a familiar form.
Consider death as a transfer of elements.
shortened: His death, therefore, consists of the dispersion of these elements. The elements, though, remain and do not disappear. In this case, life consists of composition and death consists of dispersion and the transition of elements from one state to another.

order.why: Read transformation across the kingdoms of nature.
shortened: So to speak, when the atom entered into the composition of the tree, it died to the mineral kingdom, and when consumed by the animal, it died to the vegetable kingdom, and so on until its transference or transmutation into the kingdom of man; but throughout its traversing it was subject to transformation and not annihilation. Death, therefore, is applicable to a change or transference from one degree or condition to another.

order.why: Distinguish change of form from becoming nothing.
Hear the concise account of elements returning.
Read the body’s return alongside the kingdoms of nature.
Distinguish contingent transformation from divine existence.
Explore existence and nonexistence as relative descriptions.
shortened: The stone and the man both exist, but in relation to man the stone has no existence or being. For when man dies and his body is disintegrated and destroyed, it becomes like the stone, the earth and the mineral. It is therefore clear that even though the mineral exists, it is non-existent in relation to man.

order.why: Read the related comparison between mineral and human existence.
Introduce composition and decomposition as conditions of nature.
Hear the concise relation between combination and existence.
Join the account of physical life with the analogy of concord.
shortened: Every created thing in the contingent world is made up of many and varied atoms, and its existence is dependent on the composition of these. In other words, through the divine creative power a conjunction of simple elements taketh place so that from this composition a distinct organism is produced. The existence of all things is based upon this principle. But when the order is deranged, decomposition is produced and disintegration setteth in, then that thing ceaseth to exist. That is, the annihilation of all things is caused by decomposition and disintegration. Therefore attraction and composition between the various elements is the means of life, and discord, decomposition and division produce death.

order.why: Describes composition and decomposition as the basis of bodily existence and dissolution.
Consider the diversity of forms within an ordered creation.
Read beings as gatherings of primal elements.
shortened: God hath created no being but that its existence doth depend upon the association, composition, and intermingling of simple, primal elements---whereas all that God hath decreed of death, destruction, and extinction occurreth by way of the dissolution, separation, dispersion, and dissociation of the principal constituent parts. Whensoever the natures and elements are gathered, joined, paired, and intermingled, a living being or composite entity is formed, fashioned, and brought into existence.

order.why: Consider the forms that different combinations produce.
shortened: Existence is the expression and outcome of composition and combination. Nonexistence is the expression and outcome of division and disintegration. If we study the forms of existence in the material universe, we find that all created things are the result of composition. Material elements have grouped together in infinite variety and endless forms. Each organism is a compound; each object is an expression of elemental affinity.
Life is, therefore, the product of composition; and death signifies decomposition.

order.why: Look closely at the examples of flower and wood.
shortened: Composition is the means and cause of life and decomposition is the cause of death. Now several elements are composed and united and form this flower, and so several elements are composed and the body is formed, and so with everything.

For instance, in this wood there are molecules. These molecules are gathered together and composed, then wood will be found. All substance gets its life from unification and composition and when separation takes place among these molecules, death is certain.

order.why: Follow the flower through separation.
Consider the continuing rhythm of creation and destruction.
Keep the fading plant within its devotional setting.
Read both composition and decomposition in relation to divine will.
Consider perishable forms and enduring elements.
Keep the historical claim about indestructibility in its source’s terms.
Retain the alchemical description as a historical source.
Read the terminology of growth in its original conceptual setting.
shortened: Just as there has been a process of composition, there is also of necessity a process of decomposition.

For every organic and inorganic matter there are two ways of growth - longitudinal and horizontal. When mineral substances are decomposed and then those decomposed atoms go into the makeup of other mineral organisms - this is called longitudinal growth; but when those decomposed mineral matters go into the composition of vegetable life - it is called horizontal growth.

order.why: Hear the materialist professor’s reported position within the dialogue.
Introduce the argument distinguishing accidental, necessary, and voluntary composition.
shortened: Now, formation is of three kinds and of three kinds only: accidental, necessary and voluntary. The coming together of the various constituent elements of beings cannot be accidental, for unto every effect there must be a cause. It cannot be compulsory, for then the formation must be an inherent property of the constituent parts and the inherent property of a thing can in no wise be dissociated from it, such as light that is the revealer of things, heat that causeth the expansion of elements and the solar rays which are the essential property of the sun.

The third formation remaineth and that is the voluntary one, that is, an unseen force described as the Ancient Power, causeth these elements to come together, every formation giving rise to a distinct being.

order.why: Follow the related reasoning from composition toward will.
shortened: Then what have we left as a form of composition? It is the voluntary form of composition, which means that composition is effected through a superior will, that there is will expressed in this motive or action. It is thus proved that the existence of phenomena is effected through the eternal Will, the Will of the Living, Eternal and Self-subsistent, and this is a rational proof concerning composition whereof there is no doubt or uncertainty.

order.why: Read that argument in a dialogical form.
Consider the extended presentation and its physical assumptions.
shortened: On the other hand those who are informed of divine philosophy answer in the following terms:  Composition is of three kinds.
1. Accidental composition.
2. Involuntary composition.
3. Voluntary composition.
There is no fourth kind of composition.

While we observe that after each composite organism, there is a process of decomposition we learn that the composition of the organisms of life is neither accidental nor involuntary. Then what have we as a form of composition? It is the third, that is the voluntary composition. And that means that the infinite forms of organisms are composed through a superior will, the eternal will, the will of the living and self-subsistent Lord.
This is a rational proof, that the Will of the creator is effected through the process of composition.

order.why: Read the appeal to natural order and the limits of human making.
shortened: Creation means that from every natural composition a living thing comes into existence, while from a chance composition no living thing will appear. So, for example, if man, with all his astuteness and intelligence, were to gather together and combine certain elements, a living being will not be brought into existence as it would not be according to the natural order.
But a composition made by man produces nothing because man cannot create life.

order.why: Attend to the source’s qualified use of pantheistic language.
Turn from cosmic order toward the temporal body.
shortened: As for the material station, it has an origin in time, for it is composed of the elements, and every composition must ultimately be decomposed. It is indeed impossible for composition not to be followed by disintegration.

order.why: Read the body as a compound subject to separation.
shortened: The corporeal station is human in nature and is subject to disintegration, for it is an elemental composition and that which is composed of elements must of necessity be decomposed and dispersed.

order.why: Consider illness and decomposition within bodily life.
shortened: Moreover, every composition of elements must eventually become decomposed, and this decomposition is inevitable. These sicknesses and ailments are the causes of dissolution. Otherwise the bodily composition of man would be preserved and never cease to exist.

order.why: Hear the contrasting image of elements at war.
Recognize the stated limit of thought or prayer concerning bodily permanence.
Distinguish the composite body from the spirit described as one essence.
Read the same distinction while retaining its historical enumeration of elements.
shortened: This human nature is composed of the elements. And no doubt for all the material or elemental composition there is a disintegration. But it is not composed of one element. Over 17 elements have gone into the composition of matter. Being composed of divergent elements, it is necessarily exposed or subjected to decomposition; becomes disintegrated. But the ideal nature, being an indestructible Spirit, and being one and unique in nature, being absolute radiance, the sublimity of the human nature is eternal and permanent, and it is not to be subject to disintegration.

order.why: Return to coordination among contingent beings.
Connect cohesion with the appearance of life.
shortened: All created things are expressions of the affinity and cohesion of elementary substances, and nonexistence is the absence of their attraction and agreement.

order.why: Consider physical affinity as a recurring image.
Follow the movement from atomic affinity toward spiritual relationship.
shortened: If the atoms which compose the kingdom of the minerals were without affinity for each other, the earth would never have been formed, the universe could not have been created. Because they have affinity for each other, the power of life is able to manifest itself, and the organisms of the phenomenal world become possible. When this attraction or atomic affinity is destroyed, the power of life ceases to manifest; death and nonexistence result.
It is so, likewise, in the spiritual world.

order.why: Read fellowship through the image of elements forming something new.
Hear the brief identification of life with composition.
Examine the passage’s transition into a social analogy.
shortened: Consider how clearly it is shown in creation that the cause of existence is unity and cohesion and the cause of nonexistence is separation and dissension.
Throughout all creation, in all the kingdoms, this law is written: that love and affinity are the cause of life, and discord and separation are the cause of death.

order.why: Consider how the analogy moves from leaf and stone toward human unity.
shortened: Therefore it is most evident that composition or organization and union are perpetuation of species. When the composition, or rather, compound is subjected to a flaw in the agreement (of the elements) separation and dissolution result. Therefore, it is plain and evident, that agreement and union among men are productive of life results. Every movement which aims at separation, causes disagreement and produces dissension amongst men, is to be condemned and rejected.

order.why: Read concord and separation as conditions of collective life.
shortened: O honoured lady! Look about thee at the world: here unity, mutual attraction, gathering together, engender life, but disunity and inharmony spell death. When thou dost consider all phenomena, thou wilt see that every created thing hath come into being through the mingling of many elements, and once this collectivity of elements is dissolved, and this harmony of components is dissevered, the life form is wiped out.

order.why: End the linked readings with the image of a gathering that gives life.
Retain the supplied statement concerning the end of composite things.

questions: How can decomposition be both a loss and a condition for new forms of life?
What distinctions do the passages make between a body, its elements, and the spirit?
How do the arguments from composition toward divine will work, and what assumptions do they ask a reader to consider?
What can Plato’s distinction between composite and uncompounded things clarify, and where do the two presentations differ?
What does the analogy between physical cohesion and social unity illuminate, and where might it cease to be helpful?
How might these readings deepen a conversation about grief, transformation, and the relationships that sustain a community?

references.label: 1 · Plato, Phaedo 78c–80b · What is liable to dissolution?
references.note: In Benjamin Jowett’s translation, Socrates asks whether composite things are liable to dissolution and whether what remains unchanging is more likely uncompounded. He then compares body and soul with the visible and invisible. Read the argument beside the compilation’s distinctions between bodily composition and spirit, attending to the reasoning and its assumptions rather than treating either passage as a modern scientific demonstration.

subjects.displayTitle: The divine attributes: naming what exceeds our knowledge
subjects.introduction: Pick up a flower and try to say what it is. Colour, scent and shape come readily; the reality beneath them does not, and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá uses that ordinary failure to open the hardest question. If we know even a petal only by its qualities, what are we doing when we call God knowing, powerful, living or one? Bahá’u’lláh and the Báb answer with a steadying distinction: some attributes are nothing other than the divine Essence itself, eternal and prior to any object known or ruled, while others name God’s action toward creation. To say Creator is already to speak of creatures. The distinction guards against a God assembled from parts, or merely ourselves enlarged, while leaving room to recognise His signs in creation and in the Manifestations, mirrors of a sun that never descends into the glass. Maimonides’ argument for attributes that exclude imperfection without introducing plurality offers a philosophical companion [1]. From here the way leads toward the unknowability of God, the meanings of divine oneness, and the names and attributes through which He is still praised.
subjects.arc: Begin with the limits of ordinary knowledge, distinguish essential and actional attributes, and explore recognition without claiming to comprehend the divine Essence.

order.why: Distinguish essential knowledge from knowledge considered through created objects.
shortened: Furthermore, knowledge is of two kinds: One knowledge relates to the Divine Essence - it is essential divine knowledge, identical with the Essence, not distinct from it, for in that station there is pure unity, and the Essence comprises all names and attributes. That essential divine knowledge is incomprehensible. The other knowledge is in the realm of action, meaning it is identical with what is known, and that is realization externally.

order.why: Open with the familiar example of a flower’s qualities.
shortened: When we consider the world of existence, we find that the essential reality underlying any given phenomenon is unknown. Phenomenal, or created, things are known to us only by their attributes. Man discerns only manifestations, or attributes, of objects, while the identity, or reality, of them remains hidden. For example, we call this object a flower. What do we understand by this name and title? We understand that the qualities appertaining to this organism are perceptible to us, but the intrinsic elemental reality, or identity, of it remains unknown.

order.why: Extend the distinction between qualities and essence.
shortened: As our knowledge of things, even of created and limited ones, is of their attributes and not of their essence, how then can it be possible to understand in its essence the unbounded Reality of the Divinity? For the inner essence of a thing can never be known, only its attributes. For example, the inner reality of the sun is unknown, but it is understood through its attributes, which are heat and light. The inner essence of man is unknown and unfathomed, but it is known and characterized by its attributes.

order.why: Introduce relational language through Creator, Provider, and Love.
Set out the relation of essential attributes to the divine Essence.
shortened: The Invisible and Inaccessible can never be known; the absolute Essence can never be described.

It is not that we can understand His knowledge, His sight, His hearing, His power or His life as they are in themselves: This is assuredly beyond our comprehension, for the essential names and attributes of God are identical with His Essence, and His Essence is sanctified above all understanding. If the essential attributes were not identical with the Essence, then there would be a multiplicity of pre-existences and the distinction between the Essence and the attributes would therefore also be firmly established and pre-existent. But this would imply an infinite chain of pre-existences, which is an evident error.

order.why: Hear the Bab’s distinction between essential and actional names.
shortened: Similarly befitting unto God, glorified and exalted be He, are all the attributes of perfection and names of glory, and whatsoever name is attributed to Him pertaineth to the modes of His action, and these are the modes of His command. The names of the Divine Essence have ever described God, and the names of Divine Action shall forever glorify God. Yet the former is eternally ancient, while the latter is mentioned in connection with creation and origination.

That whereby God is described in terms of knowledge is other than what ye describe. That which is described as God's hearing is other than what you describe. That which is described as God's sight is other than what you describe. And likewise you witness in all that is attributed to God.

order.why: Read essential knowledge through the cited tradition.
shortened: He was, in the pre-eternity of pre-eternities, All-Knowing, without the existence of an object known. Whoso maketh a distinction, within the Essence, between Life and Knowledge hath verily strayed, for within the Essence there is no differentiation -- according to the purport of the tradition recorded in al-Kafi, wherein the Imam declared: "God, exalted and glorified, hath ever been Lord; Knowledge is His very Essence without an object known; Hearing is His Essence without an object heard; and Sight is His Essence without an object seen; and power is His essence with nothing over which to exercise power. When He brought things into being, knowledge occurred between Him and the known, hearing between Him and the heard, sight between Him and the seen, and power between Him and that over which power was exercised."

order.why: Consider knowledge in relation to creation.
Guard against treating attributes as distinct entities before creation.
shortened: In this station, the attributes and names are not distinct from the Essence, and the realities of known things remain in the concealment of non-existence. Rather, the attributes are identical with the Essence, without any trace of distinction. Indeed, all are conditions considered within the Essence in a mode of simplicity and unity, without any trace of otherness. This is the station concerning which He, peace be upon Him, said: "God was, and there was nothing else besides Him."

order.why: Read identity of attributes and Essence without claiming knowledge of how.
Consider what familiar names affirm and what they exclude.
Hear the explanation of language adapted to created understanding.
Recognize the need to use terms without exhausting their meaning.
shortened: We refer to Him as Self-Existent because we need to make use of a term but we do not mean that that Being can be contained within our comprehension. What is intended is the Reality from Whom all things emanate, the Reality through Whom all things exist.

order.why: Read the limits of attributes inferred from observation.
shortened: There is no doubt that these infinite beings and the association of these diverse elements arranged in countless forms must have proceeded from a Reality that could in no wise be bereft of will or understanding. This is clear and proven to the mind and no one can deny it. It is not meant, however, that that Universal Reality or the attributes thereof have been comprehended. Neither its Essence nor its true attributes hath any one comprehended.

As it hath previously been mentioned, these attributes and perfections that we recount of the Divine Essence, these we have derived from the existence and observation of beings, and it is not that we have comprehended the essence and perfection of God.

order.why: Follow the extended argument concerning Essence, will, and names.
shortened: Rather, in truth His holy Essence has no attribute other than His Essence. And the attributes which the Holy Household, peace be upon them, have explained are, by the explicit word of His Holiness Rida, peace be upon him, for sweeping away delusions. God has ever been Knowing while nothing was known with Him. His Knowledge is His Essence.
All attributes are but mention of the existence of His Will. All names are but the name of His Purpose. He is sanctified from all else besides Himself through His own Essence.

order.why: Keep the recognition of created will distinct from comprehension of Essence.
Read essential eternity beyond created knowledge.
Consider lordship without a subject in the source’s theological sense.
Explore the discussion of unity and knowledge without reducing it to an equation.
shortened: Since it has been established that knowing the Essence of the Absolute is impossible then knowing the Knowledge which is identical to the Essence of the Absolute is also impossible since [we have already shown that] no difference whatsoever exists between the Essence and the Attributes.  And so in this respect no-one can penetrate that Knowledge which is identical to the Essence in order to be able to determine the relationship between the Knowledge of the Absolute and things, whether it calls for objects of knowledge or not; whether it is dependent on the realities and potentialities of things or not.  Certainly knowledge without an object of knowledge is not possible in the contingent world, but no-one knows [how the matter stands within] the Essence [of the Absolute].

order.why: Question both plurality and numerical singleness as descriptions of God.
shortened: Question: What is the meaning of the Trinity and of its three Persons?

Answer: The reality of the Divinity is sanctified and exalted beyond the comprehension of all created things, can in no wise be imagined by mortal mind and understanding, and transcends all human conception. That reality admits of no division, for division and multiplicity are among the characteristics of created and hence contingent things, and not accidents impinging upon the Necessary Being.

The reality of the Divinity is sanctified above singleness, then how much more above plurality. For that divine reality to descend into stations and degrees would be tantamount to deficiency, contrary to perfection, and utterly impossible.

order.why: Read the meaning of one beyond counting.
Consider aloneness beyond the opposition of one and two.
shortened: Into the abyss (primal depths) of the aloneness of God sink all duality, plurality and individuality.

order.why: Examine the limits of an imagined conception of unity.
shortened: And if I attempt to describe Thee by glorifying the oneness of Thy Being, I soon realize that such a conception is but a notion which mine own fancy hath woven, and that Thou hast ever been immeasurably exalted above the vain imaginations which the hearts of men have devised.

order.why: Hear the related warning about comprehending oneness.
shortened: From eternity Thou hast, in Thy transcendent oneness, been immeasurably exalted above Thy servants' conception of Thy unity, and wilt to eternity remain, in Thine unapproachable singleness, far above the praise of Thy creatures.

All who adore Thy unity have been sore perplexed to fathom the mystery of Thy oneness, and all have confessed their powerlessness to attain unto the comprehension of Thine essence and to scale the pinnacle of Thy knowledge.

order.why: Read the exclusions of how, where, name, and attribute.
Attend to the radical language of the unknowable Essence.
shortened: To every discerning and illumined heart it is evident that God, the unknowable Essence, the divine Being, is immensely exalted beyond every human attribute, such as corporeal existence, ascent and descent, egress and regress. Far be it from His glory that human tongue should adequately recount His praise, or that human heart comprehend His fathomless mystery. He is and hath ever been veiled in the ancient eternity of His Essence, and will remain in His Reality everlastingly hidden from the sight of men.
And wert thou to soar in the holy realm of "God was alone, there was none else besides Him," thou wilt find in that Court all these names utterly non-existent and completely forgotten.

order.why: Read the denial of attributes within its mystical setting.
shortened: Nay rather, the denizens of the city of immortality, who dwell in the celestial garden, see not even "neither first nor last": They fly from all that is first and repulse all that is last. For these have passed over the worlds of names and, swift as lightning, fled beyond the worlds of attributes. Thus is it said: "The perfection of belief in Divine Unity is to deny Him any attributes." And they have made their dwelling-place in the shadow of the Divine Essence.

order.why: Consider names and praise as created expressions.
shortened: Were I to attempt to describe Thee by Thy names, I would readily recognize that the kingdom of these names is itself created through the movement of Thy fingers, and trembleth for fear of Thee. And were I to venture to extol Thine attributes, I would be forced to admit that these attributes are Thine own creation, and lie within Thy grasp.

order.why: Distinguish the signs of Godhead from the Essence itself.
shortened: Say:  Lordship is My Name, whereof I have created manifestations in the world of being, while We Ourself remain sanctified above them, would ye but ponder this truth.  And Godhead is My Name, whereof We have created exponents whose power shall encompass the people of the earth and make them true worshippers of God, could ye but recognize it.  Thus should ye regard all Our Names, if ye be endued with insight.

order.why: Read loftiness as a title called into being through the Word.
shortened: Nay, loftiness and sublimity are themselves the creations of His Word, if ye choose to see with My sight not with yours.

order.why: Consider the related treatment of greatness.
shortened: Far greater art Thou than the Great One men are wont to call Thee, for such a title is but one of Thy names all of which were created by a mere indication of Thy will.

order.why: Hear the distinction between divine perception and created embodiments.
Read the dependence of created existence.
shortened: Who is there, O my Lord, that, when Thou revealest the first glimmerings of the signs of Thy transcendent sovereignty and might, hath the power to claim for himself any existence whatever? Existence itself is as nothing when brought face to face with the mighty and manifold wonders of Thine incomparable Self.

order.why: Turn toward signs and the nearness of the Manifestations.
Consider the mirror and sun without imagining the sun’s descent.
shortened: Thus, among created beings, man is the most perfect of creatures. By man is meant the perfect individual, and that perfect individual is like a mirror wherein divine perfections appear and are visible. However, the Sun does not descend from its height of sanctity and enter into the mirror, but when the mirror is pure and faces the Sun of Reality, the perfections of the Sun of Reality - which are its rays and heat - become manifest and visible in that mirror.

order.why: Distinguish personality in the Manifestation from the divine Essence.
shortened: Thou hast written concerning the Impersonality of the Divinity. Personality is in the Manifestation of the Divinity, not in the Essence of the Divinity.

order.why: Distinguishes will as an attribute of action from the Divine Essence.
Read recognition through the Manifestation alongside transcendence.
shortened: And despite His manifestation in all things, He hath ever been sanctified above them and exalted beyond that which the people of mystical knowledge have uttered. Whoso hath recognized Him in His Manifestation hath attained unto Divine Unity, and whoso hath remained heedless is of the people of the veil.

order.why: Keep the distinction of essential and acquired infallibility in its setting.
shortened: Know that infallibility is of two kinds: infallibility in essence and infallibility as an attribute. The same holds true of all other names and attributes: for example, there is the knowledge of the essence of a thing and the knowledge of its attributes. Infallibility in essence is confined to the universal Manifestations of God, for infallibility is an essential requirement of their reality, and the essential requirement of a thing is inseparable from the thing itself.

order.why: Read change and abrogation in relation to contingent conditions.
shortened: Answer: The changing and transformation of conditions and the succession and revolution of ages are among the essential requirements of the contingent world, and essential requirements cannot be separated from the reality of things. Thus it is impossible to separate heat from fire, or wetness from water, or the rays from the sun, for these are essential requirements. And since change and transformation are among the requirements of all contingent things, the commandments of God are also changed in accordance with the changing times.

order.why: Return to the signs of eternity and unity within creation.
Hear the pen’s inability to make praise adequate.
shortened: And at whatever time my pen ascribeth glory to any one of Thy names, methinks I can hear the voice of its lamentation in its remoteness from Thee, and can recognize its cry because of its separation from Thy Self.

order.why: Let the linked sequence end in the humility of prayer.
shortened: Let him then kneel and, bowing his forehead to the ground, say:

Too high art Thou for the praise of those who are nigh unto Thee to ascend unto the heaven of Thy nearness, or for the birds of the hearts of them who are devoted to Thee to attain to the door of Thy gate.  I testify that Thou hast been sanctified above all attributes and holy above all names.

order.why: Retain the supplied account of attributes with its visible source limitations.
shortened: Be thou apprised also that the manifold realms of names and attributes can never be identified with His Essence, inasmuch as His most august attributes constitute His very Essence and none else save God can ever fathom this mystery.... Moreover, all these names and attributes are applicable to His Prophets, His Messengers and His chosen ones, for they are the sanctified Mirrors reflecting the divine attributes, and the Exponents that reveal His Name; for God -- glorified is He -- is unknowable in His exalted essence and attributes, therefore His Prophets are the Bearers of His most excellent names and the embodiments of His sublime attributes, that haply no one in the kingdom of names may be deprived of recognizing these heavenly attributes....

order.why: Read the supplied statement about coexistent essential attributes.
Keep the account of theological schools attributed to its secondary source.
Consider the movement from denying attributes toward recognition.
Read names and creation through the language of Word and Will.
Distinguish the secondary discussion of actional attributes.
Read the reported problem of attributes and immutability in its historical setting.
Keep the discussion of Shaykh Ahmad’s distinction in its attributed voice.
Hear the supplied exposition of will and the limits of causal description.
shortened: God, verily, created the Will from nothing through itself, then He created through it all that to which the name "thing" can be applied. The cause of its existence, in truth, is its own self and naught else. Those who believe that the Essence is the cause of creation have made themselves partners with Him, as He cannot be known.

He hath ever been the All-Knowing, even though nothing was with Him; and He is now the All-Knowing, despite the fact that nothing is with Him in His exalted station. The attributes of power and knowledge, and all the other names and attributes, are signs belonging to His creation and the musings of the imaginations of His servants that they may not doubt their Creator in anything.

order.why: Distinguish the Primal Utterance from the unknowable Essence.
shortened: Concerning thy question about the meaning of the philosopher's saying, "From the One proceedeth only One": The statement is incorrect when the Cause is meant to be the Absolute Essence... However, when the intention behind the statement is to refer to the Primal Utterance, which is created by God by Itself, for Itself, then verily it is the truth...

There is no doubt that the Eternal Essence hath ever been immeasurably exalted above any association with His creatures; how much less could it become the source out of which things proceed. Though the statement is discussed in philosophy, the truth is that it must refer to the grades of the creative Action itself.

order.why: Retain the supplied prayer and its incomplete reference visibly.
Read the supplied emphasis on unknowability beyond singleness.
Open a comparative path through the named and unnamed in the Dao De Jing.
Read its related language of what eludes sense perception.
Keep Zhuangzi’s description within its distinct philosophical setting.
shortened: The Way has its reality and its signs but is without action or form. You can hand it down but you cannot receive it; you can get it but you cannot see it. It is its own source, its own root.

It exists beyond the highest point, and yet you cannot call it lofty; it exists beneath the limit of the six directions, and yet you cannot call it deep. It was born before Heaven and earth, and yet you cannot say it has been there for long; it is earlier than the earliest time, and yet you cannot call it old.

order.why: Consider the Upanishadic practice of negation without equating traditions.
Hear the supplied Plotinian caution concerning names.
End with the distinction between the One and self-thinking Intellect.

questions: What does the difficulty of knowing an ordinary thing’s essence suggest about claims to comprehend God?
How do the distinctions between essential and actional attributes shape the meaning of knowledge, power, or life?
What problems arise when divine oneness is understood as numerical singleness or as a collection of qualities?
How does Maimonides’ use of negative attributes compare with the affirmations and negations in these readings?
How can signs in creation and the Manifestations support recognition while leaving the divine Essence beyond comprehension?
What might intellectual humility look like in prayer, interreligious conversation, or the use of familiar names for God?

references.label: 1 · Maimonides, Guide for the Perplexed I.58 · Negative attributes
references.note: In this chapter’s English text, Maimonides argues that negative attributes can exclude imperfection without introducing plurality into the divine Essence. Language about divine qualities may describe actions or deny their opposites. Compare this approach with the compilation’s essential and actional distinctions, asking what each permits a person to say and what remains beyond the claim to know.

subjects.displayTitle: Unity of thought: deliberation, purpose, and common action
subjects.introduction: In a watchmaker’s shop one person makes the hands, another polishes, another paints, and the watch is perfected because no one tries to do everything. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá used that homely example to show that unity of thought is not sameness but the gathering of different capacities into one purpose. The members of a council must speak their minds with complete freedom, and no one may belittle another’s view; yet once a decision is reached, all must carry it out together, even to the startling point that a united wrong decision is better than a right one held in discord, because in unity the wrong will be corrected. Until minds are united, He says, nothing important, not even peace, can be accomplished. Paul asked the Philippians for the same thing, one accord and one mind joined to humility and care for others [1]. From here the path leads into consultation, the value of diversity of thought and belief, and the love among friends that makes unity in diversity more than a phrase.
subjects.arc: Begin with difference serving a shared purpose, examine consultation and common action, and return to the practices that sustain agreement and permit correction.

order.why: Establish freedom of expression and the rejection of belittling.
shortened: They must in every matter search out the truth and not insist upon their own opinion, for stubbornness and persistence in one's views will lead ultimately to discord and wrangling and the truth will remain hidden. The honored members must with all freedom express their own thoughts, and it is in no wise permissible for one to belittle the thought of another, nay, he must with moderation set forth the truth, and should differences of opinion arise a majority of voices must prevail, and all must obey and submit to the majority.

order.why: Open with different workers contributing specialized skills to a common undertaking.
Join differences of thought with a shared purpose.
shortened: Therefore, gather all different thoughts together and unite diverse concerns into a single purpose and aim, that you may fulfill the duties of servitude at the Sacred Threshold.

order.why: Face the demanding claim about unity and an erroneous decision.
shortened: If they unite on a matter and it is wrong, it is better than if they differ and are right. For this discord leads to the destruction of the divine foundation, even if one of the two sides is right - yet it causes a thousand wrongs. But if they unite and both sides are wrong, because there is unity, eventually the truth will be revealed and wrong will be transformed to right.

order.why: Ask what a meeting leaves in the lives of its participants.
shortened: The object is: let the meeting be spiritual and productive of unity and harmony, so that when you leave the meeting you may feel much better than when you entered it.

order.why: Read love, liberty, and joy as conditions of fruitful effort.
shortened: Today, the greatest of all things are love, fellowship, unity, harmony, detachment, freedom, sanctification, purity, sacrifice, and the joy of God's loved ones. If perfect fellowship and pure love are not achieved, all these efforts and hardships will be wasted, and all will ultimately suffer evident loss. The purpose of the manifestation of Truth and the rising of the Sun of Reality is the triumph of the light of God's love, so that the darkness of discord and dissension may vanish from the horizons and spiritual unity may appear. All the friends are as one soul, and all names and attributes are expressions of one person.

order.why: Connect unity of thought with world undertakings and freedom.
Place peace in relation to minds and consciences.
shortened: But the wise souls who are aware of the essential relationships emanating from the realities of things consider that one single matter cannot, by itself, influence the human reality as it ought and should, for until the minds of men become united, no important matter can be accomplished. At present universal peace is a matter of great importance, but unity of conscience is essential, so that the foundation of this matter may become secure, its establishment firm and its edifice strong.

order.why: Begin the wider horizon with love and fellowship for humanity.
Read a shared faith as a remedy for the world’s divisions.
shortened: That which the Lord hath ordained as the sovereign remedy and mightiest  instrument for the healing of all the world is the union of all its peoples in one universal Cause, one common Faith.

order.why: Hear the call to reconcile differences.
shortened: It is incumbent upon all the peoples of the world to reconcile their differences, and, with perfect unity and peace, abide beneath the shadow of the Tree of His care and loving-kindness.

order.why: Consider essential unity amid diverse opinions.
Read agreement on common principles among religious representatives.
Explore language as a means of mutual understanding.
Consider education and the development of public thought.
Connect human oneness with peace and well-being.
shortened: Thereby may every eye be brightened and every heart attain everlasting joy and bliss; thereby may all come together, with tranquil souls and well-assured hearts, beneath the shade of the pavilion of the oneness of humanity; and thereby may eternal peace, har-mony, welfare, and prosperity be realized on earth, for we are all the members of humankind - all the servants of one loving God.

order.why: Read the tailor’s image of nations forming one robe.
shortened: "The Kingdom of God is like a tailor, and nations and sects are like pieces of cloth or materials; each nation or sect is a special material and now the real tailor is relating or connecting these materials to each other.  We hope that before long there will be made a Divine robe out of these nations or materials.

order.why: Consider a shared undertaking through the temple example.
shortened: Because with one thought and one aim ye are engaging yourselves in the building of this temple, O ye servants and maidservants of the Merciful, know verily that this great project will be conducive to the union and affinity of all the children of man.

order.why: Bring agreement into the practice of hospitality.
shortened: The utmost effort must be exerted so that every soul who comes from the Western regions to the East experiences the utmost joy and happiness and becomes grateful and pleased with the divine friends.

order.why: Read love as the foundation of a credible example.
shortened: The Blessed Perfection came for the purpose of uniting the people, that He might link them together. For this purpose you must prove the means of unity to the inhabitants of the earth. This is His hope for you. If among yourselves there is no love, no unity, how can this become possible? Are you willing that His labors, His sorrows be in vain? All is to bring love to your hearts.

order.why: Begin the work of uniting others within one’s own relationships.
shortened: The friends must become the cause of unity among all nations and peoples on earth. They must certainly be united themselves in order to unite others. An extinguished lamp cannot light other lamps.

order.why: Describes people of diverse origins becoming united in thought and belief.
Consider fellowship as a model offered to others.
Look for the fruits of unity in actual relationships.
