shortened: And truly the fruit of the appearance and manifestation of the signs of unity is fellowship and friendship and love and oneness between the friends. If this is not achieved, the cycle yields no result and the lights of truth do not shine upon the horizons, the lamp of sanctification does not ignite and the veils of vain imaginings do not burn away. The morn of guidance spreads its lights upon the horizons only when unity of hearts is achieved.

order.why: Hear the removal of estrangement.
Read waves and melody as images of concord.
Consider the invitation to return to a shared nest.
shortened: The dispersed ones will return to the Center of Gathering and the birds will return from the meadows of the world unto the Nest of Harmony.

order.why: Extend the image across East and West.
shortened: The friends of East and West are associating with each other in perfect unity spiritually and communing in their hearts.

order.why: Read love as illumination for the world.
Let the prayer name comfort within gathering.
shortened: I beseech Thee by Thy Most Great Name to assemble them that love Thee around the Law that streameth from the good-pleasure of Thy will, and to send down upon them what will assure their hearts.

order.why: Hear the prayer for eloquence and agreement.
shortened: I ask God to adorn your heads with the pearls of His favor, to ignite in your hearts the fire of the love of God, to free your tongues in utterance of eloquent words and excellent meanings and mysteries in the gathering of the pious, to make ye roses of the paradise of El-ABHA, angels of heaven, united in opinions, harmonious in thoughts and to manifest in your faces signs of holiness of the Kingdom among the people.

order.why: Consider the stated purpose of a gathering.
shortened: Many gatherings are held in the world, but they do not have order and design and suffer from disunity of thought. Praised be God that the hearts of those assembled here are united and everyone's purpose is one and the same, with no trace of disunity in thought. I cherish the hope that day by day this gathering will grow and develop considerably, and will excel in every walk of life.

order.why: Read the strength attributed to community unity.
Connect gathering with the pursuit of peace.
Keep the historical claim about Muslim discord in its source setting.
Retain the qualified reference to commonplace unity without generalizing it.
shortened: The bait they have placed in this trap is the commonplace unity and the oneness that occurs to the minds of the masses, which remains as an old inheritance from ancient nations - despite the fact that in all divine tablets and scriptures, the explanation of unity exists with the most wonderful meanings.

order.why: Attend to differing capacities and receptivity.
Keep the brief reported counsel within its limited context.
shortened: These few days will pass away, but their import shall be remembered by God's friends in all ages and in all lands.

order.why: Read the army and weapons as a historical metaphor for unity.
Consider the strength of roots and foundation.
shortened: At present, praise be unto God, those sons and daughters of the kingdom have like unto blessed trees strengthened their roots are unaffected by the blowing of violent winds and like unto an edifice rest on solid and rocky foundation.

order.why: Explore the role of a collective center.
shortened: The need of a collective center by which these differences may be counterbalanced and the people of the world be unified is obvious.

order.why: Read a common refuge as a source of agreement.
shortened: For the sincere believers in God's unity, pure in faith, must have a unifying center, a single unifying word, a mighty fortress, an impregnable shelter, a lofty refuge, a strong wall, and a safe haven. When they take refuge in it and hasten to it, they are protected from the overwhelming calamity, the widespread attack, the great upheaval, and the mighty blow.

order.why: Consider the Word as a unifying whole.
shortened: Ye have striven to keep the Word whole and one.

order.why: Read the one Reality through the reported image of light.
Connect hearts with a common law.
shortened: O Ali! Under all conditions, exert your utmost effort to unite hearts and gather them together around the Divine Law of God's Cause.

order.why: Hear the related appeal to unity through law.
Read law together with love.
shortened: Stand firm in the Cause of God, then gather the people unto the law of His love lest they differ in the Cause of God, thy Lord and the Lord of the worlds.

order.why: Consider the declaration of one law.
shortened: Say: O people! Unite amongst yourselves and gather around the one Law - this indeed is the purpose of this Great Announcement which has appeared in truth and has stunned all who are in the heavens and the earth save a numbered few of Our knowing servants.

order.why: Hear the invitation to bring differing views toward one word.
shortened: May these differing views, God willing, come under the shade of one word.

order.why: Read the shared page as a concrete image of togetherness.
Consider the Word of Unity within fellowship.
shortened: Seek fellowship and love, all enter beneath the shade of the Word of Unity and plunge into the sea of oneness and uniqueness.

order.why: Keep the particular authority for resolving different understandings visible.
shortened: However, since understandings of recognition differ, therefore all the friends of God must refer to a single word so that all may be established under the shade of the word of unity, and that word is the statement of this servant.

order.why: Read the Covenant in relation to overcoming discord.
shortened: I hope that the love of God may become the cause of their unity and agreement, and that the power of the Covenant may remove this discord, for today no power can remove discord except the power of the Covenant of the Blessed Beauty.

order.why: Consider firmness in the Covenant as a point of convergence.
shortened: As much as you can, make souls firm in the Covenant and Testament, and through this firmness Baha'i unity will be established and different thoughts will be gathered at one point.

order.why: Read unity and perfections as evidence within that relationship.
shortened: The news of the unity, harmony and oneness of the friends and their intense endeavor to acquire spiritual and material perfections was a great cause of joy and delight. This news was in the nature of glad-tidings, for it is proof of firmness in the Covenant and Testament.

order.why: Bring the assembly’s work into the gathering of friends.
Retain the local setting of the news from Khurasan.
shortened: This news brought happiness and gladness that, praise be to God, the friends in Khurasan - in Bishru'ih, Khayru'l-Qura, Faran, Mashhad and Bajistan - are all attracted to the Beloved of the horizons and are confirmed in unity and accord.

order.why: Hear the joy caused by news of unity.
Attend to the effort to prevent a breach.
End the linked readings with the purpose of a life devoted to unity.
shortened: His days are numbered and ere long he shall return to the holy threshold of the Lord of all existence. He has had and has no purpose save to preserve the unity of God's Cause and the oneness of God's loved ones.

order.why: Begin supplied readings with friendship across differences of opinion.
Distinguish valuable deliberative differences from implementing a majority decision.
Examine the relation between collective decisions and learning through unity.
shortened: You are, undoubtedly, well familiar with the various aspects of this approach, which is built on the conviction that the path of unity is the only path that can lead to the civilization envisioned by Baha'u'llah. So strong is the emphasis on unity that, for example, once a decision has been made by an Assembly, everyone is expected to support that decision wholeheartedly, relying confidently on 'Abdu'l-Baha's assurance that, even if the decision is wrong, "as it is in unity the truth will be revealed and the wrong made right".

order.why: Read the voluntary dimension of commitment.
Acknowledge the difficulty of administrative training.
Consider responsibility in voting and maintaining harmony.
Read dissenting members’ responsibility within implementation.
Consider the humility involved in accepting a decision.
Preserve the possibility of politely requesting reconsideration.
shortened: What the Master desired to protect the friends against was continual bickering and opinionatedness. A believer can ask the Assembly why they made a certain decision and politely request them to reconsider. But then he must leave it at that, and not go on disrupting local affairs through insisting on his own views.

We all have a right to our opinions, we are bound to think differently; but a Baha'i must accept the majority decision of his Assembly, realizing that acceptance and harmony -- even if a mistake has been made -- are the really important things, and when we serve the Cause properly, in the Baha'i way, God will right any wrongs done in the end.

order.why: Make the stated right of appeal explicit.
Consider the warning against ideological factions.
Keep the reported comments on political labels distinct from an institutional ruling.
Read the refusal of sectarian accusations with its visible omission.
End with unity as a recurring beginning and goal.

questions: What does the example of specialized watchmakers suggest about the relationship between different capacities and a common purpose?
What habits make freedom of expression in consultation compatible with humility and the refusal to belittle?
How do the readings distinguish deliberation, implementation, reconsideration, and appeal?
What might be learned through a united effort that begins with an imperfect decision, and how could correction remain possible?
How does Philippians 2:1–4 connect a common mind with attention to others, and what does that add to this compilation?
What practical changes in a meeting, institution, or friendship might allow unity to become more than agreement in words?

references.label: 1 · Philippians 2:1–4 · A common mind and concern for others
references.note: The King James Version connects being of one accord and one mind with freedom from vainglory, humility, and attention to the interests of others. Compare these dispositions with consultation and common action in the compilation. The letter addresses a Christian community in its own setting; it offers a comparison of relational habits rather than a description of Baha’i administrative procedures.

subjects.displayTitle: False claims to religious authority: discernment and humility
subjects.introduction: Wolves, one Tablet warns, put on the shepherd’s garment, and thieves show themselves in the form of watchmen. Every age meets those who speak eloquently of God and then use that very praise as a snare, who claim hidden knowledge, take people’s wealth in the name of revelation, or circulate forged letters. Bahá’u’lláh offers clear guards against such confusion: turn to the Book and to those who serve it, rather than to those who announce their own learning; believe not every speaker; and know that anyone who claims a fresh revelation before a full thousand years have passed speaks falsely, though the door of repentance stays open even to him. Jesus, in Matthew, taught that a tree is known by its fruits [1], and conduct remains a telling witness. Yet discernment is no license for harshness, and the same Writings counsel kindness toward those who err. The inquiry leads to the long span of this Dispensation and the revelations still to come, to the emptiness of borrowed learning, and to the pride that hides inside claims of secret insight.
subjects.arc: Begin with evidence and conduct, examine the explicit temporal safeguard and historical cases, and conclude with humility, kindness, and the possibility of return.

order.why: Ask how a speaker is to be discerned beyond appearances.
shortened: This blessed word hath shone forth from the dayspring of the heaven of utterance, written to one of the loved ones - exalted be His utterance: "Believe not every speaker, trust not in every newcomer, enter not every house, and hearken not unto every claimant." For it hath been observed and continues to be observed that the liar adorns himself in the garment of truthfulness, and the one who turneth away displayeth himself in the robe of the one who advanceth.

order.why: Open with the distinction between the Book and self-appointed authority.
Introduce the practical problem of a forged anonymous letter.
Consider writings as evidence within the source’s dispute.
shortened: The writings of such fraudulent souls serve as their own exposure, and every person of understanding and insight perceives the degrees thereof. And when this detailed account was presented before the Most Holy Court, the Tongue of Grandeur spoke these words: "Souls who have been nourished by the fruits of the Supreme Pen behold themselves free from vain imaginings, confused dreams and fancies, and are so steadfast in the Cause that all the books of the world cannot turn them away from the Ancient Beauty, much less such delirious utterances."

order.why: Examine praise used to claim a higher station.
Bring the taking of money into the inquiry.
Consider the harm of false piety and pretended knowledge.
shortened: Today every falsifier layeth claim to truth, and every transgressor adorneth himself with the vesture of piety. World-consuming is the fire of the ignorant one who decketh himself with the ornament of knowledge.

order.why: Read the image of a wolf in shepherd’s clothing.
Compare a claim of association with actual deeds.
shortened: How many a servant, O my God, do we see who claims association with Thee yet speaks that which would rend the veil of Thy glory before Thy creatures, supposing himself to be of those who are righteous in Thy days. Nay, by Thy glory! Rather he hath corrupted Thy Cause and spoken that which hath caused the hearts of the sincere ones among Thy chosen ones and the near ones among Thy loved ones to burn with grief.

order.why: Test a claim of love under comfortable conditions.
shortened: Otherwise, in days of glory when the breezes of divine power are passing by, all have claimed and will claim to love the Beauty of the All-Glorious. But that claim depends upon another test, for it is not known whether the cause was outward circumstances or the Divine Spirit itself.

order.why: Preserve personal responsibility when a prominent person denies a claim.
shortened: This is the intensity of emphasis and extreme encouragement so that no one would make the excuse that such-and-such an individual is a manifest mirror, or such-and-such a soul is the embodied sign, or such-and-such a being is the personified standard, and since they did not believe, therefore we too are compelled to deny and forced to show pride.

order.why: Read the explicit thousand-year safeguard and its call to repentance.
Keep the source’s own explanation of the interval.
shortened: Even now the Ancient Pen and the Most Great Name declares: if any soul should appear with all the verses before the completion of a full thousand years - each year comprising twelve months according to what was revealed in the Qur'an, or nineteen months according to what was revealed in the Bayan where each month consists of nineteen days - you must never acknowledge him.

order.why: Read the related statement without supplying a calendar conversion.
shortened: As the Pen of the Ancient of Days and the Most Great Name now declares: should anyone appear with all the signs before the completion of a full thousand years - each year comprising twelve months according to what was revealed in the Furqan, and nineteen months according to what was revealed in the Bayan, with each month being nineteen days - you must never believe them.

order.why: Hear the concise prohibition of a premature claim.
Consider why constant new claims would obstruct establishment.
shortened: Even as in these days an unknown person in one of the cities of God laid claim, and some heedless ones were attracted, until they recognized and returned unto God and were numbered among the penitent. If it were decreed that every day a Manifestation should appear, the Cause of God would never become established.

order.why: Read the minimum interval in relation to the Cause’s establishment.
shortened: Whosoever claims this most mighty, most great, and most precious station before the completion of a thousand years hath indeed fabricated a lie against God and is of the mischief-makers, for thereby the Cause of God would be corrupted and His command would not be established among His believing servants."

order.why: Attend to the distinct context of the Bab’s Revelation.
Read the language of completion beside the explicit minimum interval.
shortened: O Dhabih! The Tongue of Grandeur proclaims: By My Self, the Truth! All Revelations have ended with this Most Great Revelation, and whoever claims after it is indeed a lying impostor. We beseech God to guide him to recant; if he repents, He is verily the Forgiver, and if he persists in what he claims, He will send against him one who will show no mercy.

order.why: Warns against subsequent claims to Revelation and calls for their retraction.
Return to the Book of Laws as the stated witness.
shortened: Know thou moreover that whosoever layeth claim to a Cause, he is a lying impostor. My Most Holy Book, which hath been sent down from My holy Kingdom as a favor unto the righteous, beareth witness unto this.

order.why: Distinguish the quantity of books from the criterion of authority.
shortened: Should anyone come with all the books in the world and speak other than what God hath willed, he is recorded as one of the people of the fire in God's Book and inscribed by the Most Exalted Pen.

order.why: Question the possession of a few words as proof of knowledge.
shortened: Of knowledge they have neither seen nor heard save a few limited words. They have taken fancy for certainty and the idol for the Eternal.

order.why: Ask what supports an asserted claim to knowledge.
shortened: They who claim knowledge without clear proof from Our presence - these are the companions of hellfire.

order.why: Keep the absence of proof visible.
shortened: Those servants who were heedless and unaware of the origin of the Cause and its foundation are now occupied with leading souls astray. Fie upon them and upon those who follow them without any clear proof or Book!

order.why: Hear the warning against believing every claim.
Consider assertions of hidden inward knowledge.
Read the reported misuse of a tradition about secret knowledge.
shortened: Regarding the matter that a believer might attain a superior understanding of realities and meanings that a learned one cannot bear to hear, and that the most special might have perceptions that the special would deny due to being veiled - such whispers come from those who wish to create a breach in God's religion, using the tradition "If Abu Dharr knew what was in Salman's heart, he would declare Salman an unbeliever" as a means. However, this tradition has a different meaning and has no connection to the fundamental beliefs of God's religion nor relation to God's Law. The reality of God's religion is one reality; at most, the difference lies in brevity and detail, in imitation and investigation.

order.why: Consider the claim concerning a sealed book.
Examine inward fantasy as a source of pretension.
shortened: Say: O friends! Ponder ye: those servants who summon the people to the dawning-place of vain imaginings are, by the life of God, neither aware nor conscious.

order.why: Distinguish pursuit of names from turning toward God.
shortened: Among the people are those who worship their own desires and imagine they worship their Ancient Lord, and among them are those who cling to a name from among the names while turning away from Him Who is named. By My life, they are all in manifest error.

order.why: Hear the related warning about imagined gods.
Consider the problem of self-authorizing claims.
Read the contradiction between claiming Truth and following desire.
shortened: Some souls attribute themselves to the Truth while they follow the desires of self and passion. I am quit of them, as every fair-minded and discerning one doth testify.

order.why: Consider usurpation carried out in the name of Truth.
Notice loyalty that lasts only while commands are welcome.
Examine flattery as a means of influence.
shortened: Despite this, some inexperienced and foolish ones wish through flattery and sweetness of speech to divert souls from the straight path and leave them wandering lost in the desert of vain imaginings.

order.why: Read the contrast of firefly and sun.
Hear Abdu’l-Baha’s rejection of claims of divinity made about him.
Distinguish the honored language of Quddus and Tahirih from a surface test of words.
shortened: For many have made claims of divinity and lordship - His Holiness Quddus, may my spirit be sacrificed for him, revealed a book on the interpretation of Samad where from beginning to end it is "I am God", and the honorable Tahirih raised "I am God" to the highest heavens in Badasht, and likewise some loved ones in Badasht, and the Blessed Beauty in the Qasidiy-i-Varqa'iyyih states: "All divinities became divine from a sprinkling of my command, and all lords became lordly from an overflow of my wisdom."

order.why: Consider the response concerning all things proclaiming God.
Preserve the catalogued Tabriz document’s attribution and editorial setting.
shortened: Certain prayers and words that have flowed from my tongue do not indicate any Cause, and whoever claims specific deputyship of the Proof of God, peace be upon Him, is a false pretender. This servant hath made no such claim, nor any other claim.

order.why: Read the reported dispute concerning Karim Khan in its own role.
shortened: Haji Mohammed Karaim Khan was a man of great influence in Persia and denied the Bab and Baha'u'llah and worked against them, writing many books, attempting at refutation and leaving no means of hate and animosity unused. His son also wrote treatises contradicting and denying the appearance of the Bab and the validity of the Manifestation.

order.why: Keep the reported theosophical claim in its historical setting.
Read the separate reported reference to Krishnamurti.
shortened: Rather, they expect that a young Indian [Krishnamurti], who at present is being groomed in Europe, will be the source of such a prodigious cause.

order.why: Consider the particular claims attributed to Kheirullah.
shortened: If Kheiruillah claims that one of the communes is written by him, do not be astonished at this. For there is an ignorant uneducated man in the United States, nay in Chicago itself who has written a pamphlet and after printing it he is circulating it abroad.

order.why: Keep the reported treatment of Bayazid and Hallaj distinct from a general account of Sufism.
shortened: Consider carefully how during the Islamic Dispensation many vainglorious men appeared who claimed the station of Divinity! What did they gain? There was a man by the name of Bayazeed who said:- 'There is no God, beside, therefore, worship me.' Again he said: 'Under my garment there is naught else save God.' Mansour Hallaj appeared and cried out:- 'I am the True One.' Every one of these leading Sufis claimed the station of Divinity, either in private or in public.

order.why: Read the criticism of self-aggrandizing incarnation claims.
Consider the reported manufacture of a prediction.
shortened: Beyond this, they even display miraculous powers, saying that soon such and such will happen. It is like someone placing gunpowder under a house and saying "Observe that soon this building will be blown away, and I am giving news of the unseen" - and then setting it on fire.

order.why: Read the specific dispute over authorship.
Retain the source’s account of earlier false claims.
shortened: In all ages there have been such false souls, as attested by the Books of God from before and after.

order.why: Consider the instability of casually asserted stations.
Read the contrast between safety and pretension.
shortened: As soon as a measure of security was established in the land, certain ignorant ones in every city laid claim to divinity. Thus from the year of the rising of the Most Great Light from the horizon of Iraq until now, numerous souls have abandoned piety and raised the standards of wickedness and rebellion, and these souls have caused upheaval and revolution in the lands. Soon you will witness that again from every land a calf will raise its call.

order.why: Keep the polemical treatment of dervish pretension attributed to its speaker.
shortened: Nevertheless, certain souls speak vain words which are but the dregs of the worthless utterances of the dervishes of old, and they glory therein. I swear by the Sun of the horizon of divine unity that such souls have never understood unity, nor have they inhaled the fragrance of the utterance of the All-Merciful.

order.why: Read the critique of Jabulqa and Jabulsa within its setting.
Consider fabricated traditions as claims to authority.
Connect those traditions with the injustice described by the source.
Read the account of fabrication contributing to persecution.
Keep the historical polemic concerning persecution in its source’s voice.
shortened: Consider the saved sect, namely the Shi'ih, who counted themselves the best of all the world's peoples. They afflicted a few helpless souls with such vain imaginings that finally they martyred the Lord of the world with hands of hatred. Now souls who have no knowledge whatsoever of the essence of this Cause have arisen with the same vain imaginings. Their purpose is to establish a region like before, and designate an illusory Jabulqa and an unknown Jabulsa.

order.why: Distinguish names from a reality not understood.
shortened: Nevertheless, they cling to a name, of whose reality none had any knowledge, while turning away from Him Who brought it into being.

order.why: Hear the image of veils being rent.
Turn toward the desires underlying an apparent allegiance.
Read the uncertainty expressed concerning an impostor.
shortened: Verily, while thou art in thy home He remembereth thee in the Most Great Prison. Be thou thankful unto God for this manifest favor. Doth it beseem anyone to deny this certainty and turn unto every doubting impostor?

order.why: Retain the concise rejection of claims.
Hear the anticipation of future pretensions.
shortened: Soon you shall hear the call from those who desire to lead the servants astray. Beware lest you follow every remote calf. Soon shall you see one who claims for himself a cause - verily he is of the liars.

order.why: Consider the cited prediction concerning claims in the Bayan.
Read steadfastness in the face of those claims.
shortened: God willing, you will remain steadfast, for false claimants have appeared and will appear in most lands. This is what the Supreme Pen foretold aforetime.

order.why: Hear the related concise counsel.
Consider the warning to guard against pretenders.
shortened: I counsel all servants and handmaidens to guard themselves against false pretenders, for We have previously announced that the cawing of the crows shall be raised.

order.why: Read the appeal for protection from claims under other names.
shortened: Those who claim to attract through any name other than this Name are belied by all atoms.
Leave those who claim of their own desires that which God hath not permitted them, then preserve souls from these ones.

order.why: Distinguish following God from following asserted authority.
Let the prayer name steadiness amid suggestions.
shortened: Enable them, moreover, O my Lord, to cleave so tenaciously to Thy Cause that they may remain unmoved by the perplexing suggestions of them who, prompted by their desires, utter what hath been forbidden unto them in Thy Tablets and Thy Scriptures.

order.why: Read steadfastness within a devotional affirmation.
shortened: Cause me, O my God, to be so steadfast in Thy love that were all who are on earth to claim the stations of Thy Cause and the conditions of Thy Manifestation, I would not turn toward them, for I bear witness that the seal of the Manifestation of God is set in this Most Great Revelation, and whosoever layeth claim to a Revelation speaketh through the promptings of self and passion.

order.why: Turn toward knowledge through the image of a replenished lamp.
Preserve the instruction to show kindness and avoid opposition to the Qadiyani.
shortened: Do not oppose the Qadiyanis. Deal with them kindly. If you can, teach that Qadiyani person with perfect love and kindness and help him understand that these efforts of yours are useless and will yield no result.

order.why: End with the possibility of repentance, return, and forgiveness.
